concerns.text: The equivalence test (TOST) compares Frozen‑Subspace OPD to the Full‑Parameter OPD baseline, but the hypothesis (US‑2) also requires assessing whether the OPD‑derived subspace is uniquely beneficial for SFT. The current design compares Frozen‑Subspace SFT only to the Full‑Parameter OPD baseline, not to a Full‑Parameter SFT baseline, which conflates effects of training objective with subspace constraints and may not isolate the geometric advantage.

Statistical power analysis for the SFT comparison re‑uses the σ=0.015 estimate from OPD literature (He 2023). This may not reflect variance in SFT performance, risking under‑powered tests. A separate power calculation based on pilot SFT runs should be performed.

The mask derivation uses parameter deltas from OPD runs that share the same training data and model as the evaluation runs, albeit with different seeds. This could introduce a subtle data‑leakage confound because the subspace may capture dataset‑specific patterns. Consider deriving masks from a held‑out subset or from a separate validation split to ensure independence.

The plan assumes all phases will complete within the 7 GB / 6 h limits on a free‑tier CPU runner. Given TinyLlama‑1.1B even with 8‑bit quantization, training for 3 epochs across 30 seeds may exceed these limits, leading to systematic failures and incomplete data, which threatens the validity of the statistical conclusions.
